 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "WASI fd_read of the 32 MiB file into linear memory", "component": "WASI fd_read", "frozen": true,
                 "why_every_version_executes_it": "cksum must see every byte, and preview1 lets file data reach the program only through fd_read",
                 "least_work": {"amount": 33554432, "unit": "bytes", "per_unit_cost_us": 0.000125,
                                "total_ms": 4.19, "calling_context": "large (>=1 MiB) sequential reads, warm cache, at the native ~8 GB/s read rate"},
                 "max_cores": 1}],
 "floor_ms": 4.19, "L_delta": -0.828,
 "rationale": "The only frozen work is fd_read of 32 MiB, about 4.2 ms on one core, well below T_R_upper = 9.59 ms (delta -0.83 < b). The CRC computation is mutable code, so it adds nothing to the floor. Wasm lacks carry-less multiply, so a fast CRC under ~12 ms is uncertain. No certificate is possible, and I cannot name a change that surely closes the gap."}
